primitives.name: Behavioral Duality Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Examining player behavior across games with different design philosophies allows us to empirically test how structural incentives interact with individual agency – insights that extend beyond games to inform our understanding of user behavior across digital systems.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B': 'Behavioral preference vector (dimensionless)', 'S': 'Structural incentive matrix (dimensionless)', 'A': 'Individual agency scalar (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players exhibit stable behavioral dispositions; structural incentives modulate but do not fully determine behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S becomes orthogonal to B, agency dominates; when S aligns with B, structure dominates.

layer2.mapping: The kernel maps behavioral trajectories across platforms via a probabilistic duality function f(B,S,A) = P(B|S,A), enabling GSI to predict cross-platform behavior.

primitives.name: Flexibility Preference Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our findings reveal that while games incentivize different behaviors (specialization in League versus flexibility in TFT) for performance-based success, players exhibit consistent behavior across platforms.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_i': 'Probability of selecting option i (dimensionless)', 'n': 'Total number of available options (dimensionless)', '\\mathcal{F}': 'Flexibility index (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Behavioral flexibility is quantifiable via entropy of choice distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \mathcal{F} approaches 0, player specializes; when \mathcal{F} approaches 1, player diversifies.

layer2.mapping: The index serves as a derived kernel in GSE's state transition model to classify player types based on strategic adaptability.

primitives.name: Structural Incentive Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper examines how players navigate two games with fundamentally different structural incentives for performance-based success: League of Legends (League) and Teamfight Tactics (TFT).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_1, S_2': 'Incentive structures of two games (dimensionless)', '\\rho': 'Alignment coefficient (dimensionless)', '\\text{Cov}': 'Covariance operator (dimensionless)', '\\sigma': 'Standard deviation operator (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Incentive structures can be quantified and compared via statistical correlation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \rho approaches 1, structures are aligned; when \rho approaches -1, structures conflict.

layer2.mapping: The alignment measure enables GSE to compute cross-game behavioral transferability by comparing structural similarity.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that player behavior under varying structural incentives reflects a dual dynamic between agency and constraint. The Behavioral Duality Kernel models this as a probabilistic function f(B,S,A) = P(B|S,A), where B represents behavioral preference, S denotes structural incentive, and A captures individual agency. This formulation implies that while structure influences behavior, it does not fully determine it. The Flexibility Preference Index quantifies this influence via entropy, allowing classification of players into flexible or specialized categories. Structural Incentive Alignment measures how closely two game environments mirror each other in shaping behavior, enabling prediction of cross-platform adaptation. Together, these primitives form a coherent framework for modeling user behavior across digital systems, grounded in empirical data from competitive gaming. Failure modes include overfitting to specific game mechanics or misinterpreting structural influence as deterministic control.
